shots.text: They marched us across the creek on a bridge made of our own dead.
shots.note: Chained trap-jaws marched over a bridge of their own dead.

shots.text: Three hundred twenty of us had become one hundred and six.
And Vask? They gave him a place in their army, the one trap-jaw with no chains.
In the fire colony, we weren't ants anymore. We were tools.
We dug their tunnels, fed their larvae, and slept in the cold chambers near the surface where the rain came in.
shots.note: Chained in the cold chamber, rain dripping in.

shots.text: Every morning a fire soldier named Kesh walked down our line and picked one of us to make an example of.
Every morning I kept my head down and let him pass.
shots.note: 250 in the line, head down, a faint green glint.

shots.text: Every night I listened to Vask laughing with the fire soldiers above us.
Because I'd learned something the night my colony fell: strength you show too early gets you killed.
I learned their scent signals. I learned which guards were lazy, which tunnels led to the queen, and which of their soldiers secretly hated each other.
They thought I was just another slave.
And one day, Vask, I'm coming for you first.
